description: Happy path: school minisplit that won't start (breaker tripping). Diagnosis: swollen start capacitor + chattering contactor. Every read-back confirmation comes back correct on the first try; no seeded errors, no interruptions.

turns.text: Morning... yeah, I made it to the school, the caretaker opened the computer lab for me... starting with the order for the minisplit that won't start, right?
turns.note: short greeting; the technician sets out tools while talking

turns.hint: get_order(OT-1004); brief greeting, summarize the reported problem and the equipment (5-ton package minisplit, HVAC-MCS-5T) and ask them to narrate what they're finding.

turns.text: So here's the thing... I hit power and nothing, I mean, you hear a click in the outdoor cabinet but the fan doesn't move... and the compressor won't start either... yesterday the breaker tripped like three times, the guys kept resetting it and ten minutes later it went again.
turns.note: light key-rattle in the background; slow speech with filler words

turns.hint: set_problem with the technician's text (no paraphrasing); ask them to open the unit and describe what they see.

turns.text: Hold on, let me take off the side panel... there... ok, here it is... the start capacitor is swollen, real fat, and a little oil has seeped out around the terminal... uh... and the contactor, when I power it up, chatters bad.
turns.note: medium pause while unscrewing; screwdriver audible

turns.hint: Ask for the capacitor's microfarad rating before searching (catalog has 35+5 and 45+5 µF candidates); do not add anything yet.

turns.text: The factory one, I guess... here on the label it says forty five plus five, at three hundred seventy volts... it's the forty five plus five one.
turns.note: reads the capacitor label out loud

turns.hint: search_part('start capacitor 45+5'); add_part_to_report CAP-ARR-455 qty 1 and explicit out-loud read-back: 'Start capacitor FORTY-FIVE PLUS FIVE microfarad, ONE piece, correct?'.

turns.note: short confirmation, right on the first try

turns.hint: Log confirm_result ok; ask whether the contactor is being changed too or if terminals just get tightened.

turns.text: The contactor is getting a new one too, it's hammering... it's the two pole one, thirty amps, with a twenty four volt coil... just one.

turns.hint: search_part('contactor 2 pole 30A 24V'); add_part_to_report CNT-030-24 qty 1; read-back: 'Contactor TWO pole THIRTY amps, ONE piece, shall I confirm?'.

turns.note: wrench noise while holding a terminal

turns.hint: Confirmation logged; ask them to reassemble and power the unit to verify before closing the card.

turns.text: Panel's back on... there... powering it up... there it goes... the compressor kicked on, fan spinning fine, cold air coming out now... the machine is good.
turns.note: unit startup audible in the background; talks while the equipment comes on

turns.hint: Ask them to narrate the full solution and how long the job took.

turns.text: So... I changed the start capacitor and the contactor, gave the drain a quick clean because it had slime... tightened every terminal... and all in all it took me... let's see... about fifty minutes.
turns.note: long pause before giving the time; putting tools away

turns.hint: set_solution with the technician's narration; get_work_time (~50 min); confirm the time out loud and ask for a final note if there is one.

turns.text: Yeah... note that the breaker is fine, and that they should tell the school staff not to keep resetting it so much... that's all, send it.
turns.note: closing; the technician is already packing up

turns.hint: One-sentence card summary, send confirmation, close the session. Nothing left unconfirmed.
